messages.subject: Recent changes in INLA
parts:
This email is to inform you about two recent changes in INLA, starting
from the testing-version of today.

* The internal graph-spesifcation has been under a major revision and
made more general. Plotting is easier. All is easier. The changes are
backward-compatible.

The FAQ page is updated

https://sites.google.com/a/r-inla.org/www/faq#TOC-Some-of-the-models-needs-a-graph-ho

on these new changes. In short,

- the argument in f(), 'graph.file', is replaced by a more general
argument 'graph', but your old code will still runs, although you will
get a warning the first time. To fix this, simply replace argument
'graph.file' with 'graph'.

- You can now specify a binary neighbour (sparse) symmetric matrix as
the 'graph' instead of a storing the graph on a file. Hopefully, this
would make it easier to convert from graph-spesifications from other
packages.


* The builds for Windows 32bit machines are now done in a 32bit
(emulator) environment, using a 32bit compiler (and not any more, as
for Linux and MaxOSX, running the 64bit compiler in a 32bit mode).
Hopefully, this will improve the stability, preliminary reports are
good.


--
